body_html:
How to think about it

Animals are supported by an exoskeleton (insects), an endoskeleton (vertebrates) or a hydrostatic skeleton (earthworms). The human skeleton supports and protects the body, allows movement, makes blood cells and stores minerals. The axial skeleton is the skull, spine and ribs; the appendicular skeleton is the limbs and girdles.

Joints may be immovable (skull), slightly movable (spine) or freely movable synovial joints (ball-and-socket in the hip, hinge in the knee). Muscles are attached to bones by tendons; ligaments join bone to bone. Arthritis damages joints; osteoporosis makes bones weak.

Example

Which joint is at the shoulder?

It moves in all directions.

Answer: a ball-and-socket joint

Example

What joins a muscle to a bone?

Not a ligament

Answer: a tendon

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up tendons and ligaments.
  • Thinking muscles push bones.
  • Thinking bones are dead tissue.

faq.q: How do the biceps and triceps move the arm?
faq.a: They are antagonistic: the biceps contracts to bend the arm, the triceps contracts to straighten it.

faq.q: How can you keep your bones healthy?
faq.a: Eat food with calcium and vitamin D and do weight-bearing exercise.

items.q: What kind of skeleton does an earthworm have?
items.e: Vertebrates have bones inside; insects, spiders and crabs have a hard case outside; worms, slugs and jellyfish have no skeleton.

items.q: What kind of skeleton does a spider have?

items.q: Which animal has an endoskeleton?

items.q: What is a joint?
c: a place where two bones meet so the body can bend
items.e: Knees, elbows and shoulders.

items.q: Which part of the body is strong bands that hold bones together at a joint?

items.q: Which part of the body is soft tissue inside some bones that makes blood cells?

items.q: Which type of joint moves backwards and forwards in one direction, like a door?

items.q: Which joint is found at the elbow and knee?

items.q: Which type of joint moves in almost every direction?

items.q: What type of joint is the shoulder?

Why do muscles work in pairs?
c: Muscles are always both pulling at once.
Muscles can only pull, so one pulls a bone one way and the other pulls it back.
items.e: Muscles pull bones by contracting. They work in pairs: when one contracts, the other relaxes.

items.q: What does a muscle do when it contracts?
c: It lets go of the bone.
It gets longer and pushes a bone.
It gets shorter and fatter and pulls on a bone.
items.e: Muscles pull bones by contracting. They work in pairs: when one contracts, the other relaxes.

items.q: When you straighten your arm, what does your triceps (back of the upper arm) do?
c: It contracts and pulls the lower arm straight.
items.e: Muscles pull bones by contracting. They work in pairs: when one contracts, the other relaxes.

items.q: Where is a ball and socket joint found in the body?
items.e: Ball and socket joint: the shoulder and hip.

items.q: What is gout?
c: an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction
loss of bone mass with age, often due to low oestrogen
inflammation of joints due to deposits of uric acid crystals
items.e: Gout: inflammation of joints due to deposits of uric acid crystals.

items.q: Which disorder is loss of bone mass with age, often due to low oestrogen?
items.e: Osteoporosis: loss of bone mass with age, often due to low oestrogen.

items.q: When the biceps contracts, what happens to the arm?
items.e: The triceps relaxes at the same time.

items.q: How does a jellyfish keep its shape without a skeleton?
c: The water around it supports its body.
items.e: Water supports it.

items.q: Where is a hinge joint found in the body?
c: the carpal and metacarpal of the thumb
items.e: Hinge joint: the knee and elbow.

items.q: Why do bones of older people break more easily?
c: they lose calcium and become less dense
items.e: Bone density decreases with age.

items.q: What is osteoporosis?
c: a disease in which bones lose minerals and become weak and break easily
items.e: It is common in older people; calcium and exercise help prevent it.

items.q: A beetle's exoskeleton does not grow. How does a growing insect manage?
c: It sheds (moults) its old exoskeleton and grows a new, bigger one.
items.e: Moulting.

items.q: What is arthritis?
c: a lack of red blood cells
inflammation of the joints, making them painful and stiff
items.e: Cartilage in the joint may wear away.

items.q: Which disorder is inflammation of joints due to deposits of uric acid crystals?
items.e: Gout: inflammation of joints due to deposits of uric acid crystals.

items.q: Why does exercise help keep bones and muscles healthy?
c: It makes muscles stronger and bones denser.
It stops blood cells being made.
items.e: Use them or lose them.

items.q: A learner asks: do people with longer legs jump further? How could they test it fairly?
c: Let everyone jump however they like.
Measure each person's leg length and jump using the same kind of jump and the same start line.
items.e: Fair test.

items.q: Why is the spine made of many small bones (vertebrae)?
c: so it is lighter than air
so the back can bend while still protecting the spinal cord
items.e: Flexible protection.

items.q: Why is the skull one hard piece but the spine is made of many small bones?
c: The skull protects the brain; the spine must bend as we move.
items.e: Shape fits the job.

items.q: Which type of joint is found in the sutures of the skull?
items.e: Fibrous (immovable) joint: the sutures of the skull.

items.q: Why do doctors put a broken arm in a cast?
c: to make the arm bend more
to stop the bone being alive
to keep the bone still so it can mend
items.e: Bones heal.

items.q: Which type of muscle is found in the walls of the intestine?
items.e: Smooth muscle is involuntary.

items.q: How could you measure the force of different muscles fairly?
c: Use the same newton meter and the same method for each muscle, and repeat.
Use a different newton meter each time.
items.e: Fair test.

items.q: Which type of joint is found in the vertebrae?
items.e: Cartilaginous joint: the vertebrae.
